body:
USER directive (2026-08-25): the product and repository are bare-metal only.
Completely remove Linux target support and Linux-specific references from the
current tracked tree.

## Existing coverage and remaining gap

#120 (“The baremetal downgrade: smallest RISC-V, no MMU, no Linux”) moved the
shipping AX7101 profile to RV32I bare metal, removed the MMU/caches, and made
the Linux-facing sound-card surface optional. That completed its stated scope,
which explicitly kept the Linux flow buildable for comparison/bring-up until
#116.

That is narrower than this directive. At `origin/dev`
`a8b27a5f503b1a9c3f267e456f4683ef35df4dc7`, a case-insensitive inventory of
`linux|ptp4l|phc2sys|rootfs|buildroot|opensbi` finds **1,197 references across
214 tracked files**. #116 and PR #228 also still describe option-OFF Linux as a
supported comparison owner. No existing open ticket owns complete removal.

## Objective

Make the current first-party `kebag-logic/milan-fpga` tree and every supported
product configuration bare-metal-only:

- no Linux kernel, rootfs, Buildroot, OpenSBI, Linux driver, device-tree boot,
  ALSA, linuxptp, or Linux-service product path;
- no shipping or comparison configuration whose runtime owner is Linux;
- no active, generated, or tracked historical documentation that presents a
  Linux target as part of this product; and
- one authoritative bare-metal firmware, boot, diagnostics, and ownership
  contract.

“Complete removal” applies to the checked-out tracked tree and generated
artifacts. Git history, closed Issue/PR discussions, and upstream/submodule
history are not rewritten.

## Scope

1. **Product/build surface**
   - Remove Linux/rootfs/Buildroot/OpenSBI/device-tree build and deploy modes,
     configs, patches, image slots, environment variables, and command-line
     options from first-party sources.
   - Make every shipping builder recipe produce the bare-metal RV32I profile
     and firmware image. Unknown legacy options fail generically; do not retain
     a dormant compatibility alias.
   - Remove Linux-only hostplane, driver, ALSA/sound-card, NAPI, ethtool, tc,
     and service hooks that have no bare-metal consumer. Preserve the fabric
     AAF/TDM/I2S/audio datapath itself.

2. **Runtime ownership**
   - Bare-metal firmware owns boot-time policy, CSR initialization, identity,
     persistence, diagnostics/UART, and any remaining software-visible
     control.
   - Fabric gPTP remains the product time-sync owner. Remove `ptp4l`,
     `phc2sys`, statd/lease mirrors, and the option-OFF Linux owner.
   - An RTL option-OFF form may remain only as an explicitly verification-only
     hardware comparison that has no Linux dependency and is not a supported
     product image.

3. **Requirements and documentation**
   - Rewrite `REQUIREMENTS.md` and active architecture, integration, boot,
     time-sync, feature-status, register-map, testing, and troubleshooting
     authorities around the bare-metal product.
   - Remove or replace obsolete Linux diagrams, generators, rendered outputs,
     findings, historical snapshots, and examples from the tracked tree. If
     historical evidence must be retained, preserve it in Git history or an
     external archive rather than leaving Linux references in the current
     checkout.
   - Update generators first; generated Markdown/SVG/drawio/config artifacts
     must not reintroduce removed text.

4. **External companion state**
   - Remove the shipping rootfs/service artifact contract and any companion
     repository dependency from product validation. If a companion repository
     still publishes Linux images, link its cleanup PR and prove the FPGA
     repository no longer consumes them.

## Relationships and lane conflicts

- Predecessor: #120, completed for the narrower shipping-profile downgrade.
- #110 and #116 must be reconciled so their acceptance no longer preserves a
  Linux comparison owner. PR #228 currently conflicts with this directive and
  must remove or supersede those claims before merge.
- #98 owns general documentation drift machinery; this ticket supplies the
  bare-metal-only product policy that machinery must enforce.
- #248/#255 can reuse the dead-code/documentation-cleanup lessons, but this is
  a product-platform migration, not a maintainability style rule and is not
  part of #258's SystemVerilog scope.
- Possible lane conflicts: #116/PR #228, builder/deploy work, documentation
  generators, and any branch changing `REQUIREMENTS.md` or bare-metal firmware.

Executor: Mister-M-alt / A4 (implementation, PR #294 at `acda62a9`); A5 (answers to the review round)
Independent reviewer: R2, consolidating cleared-context rounds R5 (RTL/#116), R6 (tooling/#259) and R7 (docs/process) on PR #294 — NEGATIVE at `acda62a9`, re-review pending. External reviewer: unassigned
Unresolved decisions: none. The supported target is bare metal only; a retained
option-OFF RTL elaboration is verification-only and cannot retain a Linux
runtime or documentation contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every shipping configuration builds and boots the bare-metal RV32I
      firmware; there is no supported Linux/rootfs image or runtime profile.
      (`--software-profile` accepts only `baremetal`, `--flashboot` only
      `none|baremetal`, five configs `fabric_gptp: true`; AX7101 cold QSPI boot
      to `Milan baremetal: fabric entity enabled` twice, 2026-09-06, PR #361
      head image VERSION 0x00020057.)
- [x] First-party Linux-specific source/config/script/patch/driver/service files
      are removed, and no generated artifact recreates them. (170 paths deleted
      in the #294 lane `59ba6ffb..40a2192a`; six retired-stack paths at
      `59ba6ffb`, zero at HEAD; generated .svg/.drawio text is scanned; docs.yml
      no-drift gates.)
- [x] The current tracked documentation and requirements describe only the
      bare-metal product. Historical Linux material is absent from the checkout
      without rewriting Git history. (REQUIREMENTS.md section 1,
      DOC_GENERATION.md Historical pages, docs/history/v1/README.md "Issue #259
      exception"; docs_check 0 findings; `git show 59ba6ffb:<path>` recovers
      the retired files.)
- [x] #110/#116 and PR #228 no longer claim Linux support or an option-OFF
      Linux owner; any retained option-OFF RTL is clearly verification-only.
      (Bodies reconciled 2026-08-26; PR #228 merged `5b680542`;
      `milan_soc.py --no-fabric-gptp` is the announced VERIFICATION-ONLY door
      and the gate refuses it elsewhere.)
- [x] Add `scripts/check_baremetal_only.py` (or an equivalently focused gate)
      that inventories all first-party tracked text, excludes only vendor/
      submodule content and its own deliberately broken fixtures, and fails on
      any target-Linux/rootfs/service reference. The clean-tree result is zero.
      (0 findings across 758 files at `7fd04d45`; hosted in docs.yml.)
- [x] The gate's self-test proves every prohibited term and path class fails,
      proves generated outputs are scanned, and proves a missing/unreadable
      inventory is a failure rather than a zero count. (336 arms PASS at
      `7fd04d45`; per-term loops; `term-in-generated-svg`; empty, missing and
      unreadable inventory arms exit 2.)
- [x] Bare-metal firmware/builder focused tests, documentation/path/generator
      checks, Behave, lint/xvlog, the complete Verilator suite, and complete
      Yosys portability gate pass on the merged tree `7fd04d45`. (Hosted docs
      34056859720, elaborate 34056859560, rtl-fast 34056859544 and rtl-full
      34056859527 green; `scripts/xvlog_gate.py --check` PASS at the ratchet on
      the bench box; local records in PR #294 at `32b57f17` and PR #361.)
- [x] A booted shipping board demonstrates bare-metal startup and
      UART/diagnostic access without a kernel, rootfs, or Linux service
      artifact. (2026-09-06, PR #361 head image VERSION 0x00020057, AEM CRC
      e825b108, QSPI layout `{bitstream, aem}`; grader `id-miln`,
      `version-gptp-publication`, `aem-image`, `fabric-enabled`,
      `clkv-fabric-owner`, `phc-advances` PASS after two cold cycles and after
      90 s.)

Booted-board remainder, re-homed to milestone 3 (Board to Board testing 1x1
TDM Milan V1.2); none of these is a Linux-removal property:

- [ ] #358 (owner): the booted shipping image reaches gPTP lock on the bench
      wire; grader `gptp-identities`, `gptp-path`, `gptp-pdelay`, `gptp-locked`
      PASS. #117 records the two-board evidence on the released image.
- [ ] #70 (owner): saved state survives a power cycle on the booted shipping
      image; the #369 writer at `82b85715` is flashed and proven on the board.
- [ ] #117 (owner): audio datapath operation on the booted shipping image once
      the controller and capture hosts that #358 reports unreachable are back.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --selftest
python3 scripts/check_baremetal_only.py --check
python3 sw/builder/test_builder.py --require-elaboration
python3 scripts/lint_rtl.py --check
python3 scripts/xvlog_gate.py --check
suite_logs=$(mktemp -d)
scripts/run_all_suites.sh "$suite_logs"
syn/yosys/run.sh
```

The PR records the exact base, head, generated-artifact revisions, candidate
tree, and booted-board image identity. Hosted checks supplement rather than
replace the local candidate results.

## Non-goals

- No Git-history rewrite or deletion of closed GitHub discussions.
- No removal of Ethernet/AVB/Milan interoperability or host-side development
  tools merely because a developer happens to run them on a Linux workstation;
  the prohibition concerns the product target, supported build/runtime paths,
  and tracked product documentation.
- No removal of the fabric audio datapath; only Linux-facing host surfaces with
  no bare-metal owner are retired.
- No unrelated HDL modernization; #253/#258 own interface and SystemVerilog
  quality rules.

comments.body:
[A2] Recording what PR #228 (the #116 fabric-publication lane) already removed under this directive, so this ticket's repository-wide sweep can subtract it:

Removed as PRODUCT paths (the lane's own surface):
- `sw/litex/deploy.sh`: the kernel/OpenSBI/DTB/rootfs flash slots, their env inputs, the DTB/`csr.csv` CSR-window preflight chain, and the live-rootfs owner prover. `flash-pair` is bare-metal `{bitstream, aem}` only; a layout naming a retired Linux image or a non-fabric owner refuses before programmer I/O.
- `sw/litex/check_gptp_owner_pair.py`: the rootfs archive/lifecycle grading role is retired explicitly (`--rootfs` is now a refused argument); the tool is the bare-metal fabric-owner and bitstream-binding preflight.
- `sw/litex/qspi_owner_transition.py`: the software owner and full/kernel-manifest profiles refuse as retired; the one planned transition is the fabric-baremetal refresh.
- `sw/litex/layout_from_soch.py`: a soc.h carrying the retired software owner or Linux flashboot constants refuses reconstruction.
- `sw/builder/endstation_builder.py`: `fabric_gptp: false` is refused for every configuration; the ptp4l fragment generator and the software-owner permission marker are deleted, and a handoff deletes stale copies of both from the sibling overlay.
- `sw/litex/milan_soc.py`: option-off decoupled from Linux; `--no-fabric-gptp` is an announced VERIFICATION-ONLY elaboration with zero gPTP owners, and its soc.h owner is `none` (nothing emits the retired `software` code any more).
- configs: every `fabric_gptp: false` comparison config flipped to the fabric owner (`endstation_arty_current/4x4/8ch`); `sweep.sh`, `build.sh`, `sweep_extra.sh` recipes carry `--fabric-gptp` only.
- Authorities rewritten to the bare-metal-only contract at the lane's surface: `REQUIREMENTS.md` (intro, gPTP bullet, 4.F/4.G retirement banners, section 5 criteria), `docs/ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md`, `docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md`, `docs/design/GPTP_PLANE.md`, `docs/integration/BAREMETAL_FIRMWARE.md`, `docs/integration/QSPI_FLASHBOOT.md` (the full-Linux layout is a retired-history section), `docs/reference/milan_feature_status.json`.

Guarding the surface: `scripts/check_baremetal_scope.py` (`--check`/`--selftest`, wired into the hosted docs job) inventories the lane's owned files and fails on any retired daemon term without a retirement anchor, any `fabric_gptp: false` in a config, or any `--no-fabric-gptp` in a launcher; a missing inventory file is a failure, not a zero count.

Still THIS ticket's (not the lane's): the repository-wide inventory and removal (Linux profile flags in `milan_soc.py`/`build.sh`, hostplane/driver/ALSA surfaces, Buildroot trees, the remaining documentation/diagram corpus, `check_dtb_csr.py` itself, companion-repo decoupling, and the full `scripts/check_baremetal_only.py` zero-reference gate with a booted-board demonstration).

Implementation is ready for review in #294 at final head `acda62a96cc55922c08519088e94a131f827c102`.

The PR makes every shipping recipe bare-metal-only, removes first-party kernel/rootfs/driver/service/host-plane/DMA/PCM-ring product paths while preserving fabric audio, and adds a fail-closed policy gate. The scanner passes 254/254 adversarial arms with 0 findings across 654 tracked first-party files. Complete exact-head validation is 50/50 Verilator suites (2,116,681 checks), 45/45 Yosys tops, and 14/14 Behave features / 312/312 scenarios.

The PR body and its review comments contain the full findings record. That includes the hosted discovery that patch `0005` had stale hunk counts after a semantic rewrite; final head repairs it, passes the complete isolated pinned-toolchain builder (including gate 23h and 3/3 mutation arms), and has a green hosted `elaborate` job.

This issue is intentionally left open while #294 is reviewed. The booted shipping-board criterion remains the physical handoff in #117, and nonvolatile restoration remains #70; #294 does not claim either result.

[A5] REVIEW READY — PR #294 at head `0cc958e4` (eight commits over `acda62a9`, base `dev` `8043f299`).

Two records this issue owns, made public here as the [R2] round required:

1. **Archive rule.** The repository rule stands: an obsolete page is never deleted — it stays at its path under `[OBSOLETE + YYYY-MM-DD]` and current pages cite it only as labelled historical evidence (now enforced by `scripts/docs_check.py` rule 7 in both docs CI jobs). #259 is the one recorded exception: pages whose subject is the retired target software stack left the tree, live in Git history at `59ba6ffb` (`git log --diff-filter=D`), and are registered in `RETIRED`. The `historical_now_obsolete/` folder closed on 2026-08-30 when this directive removed its last pages; `OPEN_SOURCE_MIGRATION.md` stays retired because it documents the Zynq PS/DMA-wrapper era and trips the bare-metal gate when restored. Two protocol pages removed in the same sweep without a retired-stack subject (`docs/testing/MILAN_COMPLIANCE_MATRIX.md`, `docs/testing/PDU_GETTER_SETTER_VERIFICATION.md`) are restored under their markers. Authority text: `docs/DOC_GENERATION.md` section 5. Recorded on the maintainer's instruction to resolve the round; the maintainer may amend it here.

2. **Scope beyond the directive, now stated.** The unattended campaign runner (`harness/`, 36 files incl. 16 target-agnostic ones) was removed rather than re-targeted because the bare-metal board exposes only the UART; successors are named in `docs/testing/TESTING.md` section 6d and on #70/#117. The dead 802.1Q/CBS + `ptp_ts` record chain, whose only source was the transmit path this directive retired, is now removed from `milan_datapath` as well (PR `[A5]` comment, [R5] MAJOR).

Role fields on this issue are filled. Finding-by-finding answers and validation are in the PR; re-review requested at `0cc958e4`.

[A8] REBASE DECISION — PR #294 onto current `dev` `24ace48ad12a3ec3eecd30331fac8a56fceb6722`

The public contracts already determine the conflict resolution:

- Preserve the current general versioned-history policy in `docs/README.md`: non-product obsolete evidence remains under `docs/history/v1` and names a current successor.
- Preserve the explicit #259 exception in `REQUIREMENTS.md` section 1 and this issue: retired target-Linux build, runtime, rootfs, driver, service, and product documentation is absent from the tracked checkout and remains recoverable only from Git history.
- Resolve the `docs/history/v1` conflicts path by path. Keep newer non-target historical material introduced on `dev`; do not restore a page whose subject is the retired target stack. Update the history index, routing metadata, retired inventory, and bare-metal scanner together so they state and enforce the same boundary.

This records the semantic rule before conflict resolution; it is not a blanket ours/theirs choice. No design decision remains open for the rebase.

[R0] PR #294 merged into `dev` at `40a2192a` (2026-09-01). The digital acceptance criteria of this issue and #116 are complete on `dev`; this issue deliberately STAYS OPEN for its booted-board criteria, as the PR body records ("Nothing closes: #116 and #259 keep their booted-board acceptance criteria open; #117 owns the physical gPTP lane and #70 the persistence lane"). Recorded here so the review-integrity sweep's open-issue flag has its divergence note.

[A9] BOOTED-BOARD ATTEMPT, 2026-09-06: the shipping image does not boot from QSPI, so the last criterion stays open

Built the ship shape from `dev` 3cfc0b81 with the tracked recipe (`build.sh ax7101 --sweep`, shape gate PASS, `endstation_ax7101_1x1_tdm8`, bare-metal manifest, fabric owner). Three seeds closed timing; the AltSpreadLogic_high seed (WNS +0.330 ns) was flashed with `flash-pair` after the live QSPI bitstream was proved to be the dev-40506026 shipping build (image set written and verified in owner-safe order).

What the board did on every cold boot from QSPI (12 s and 30 s power-off), on a JTAG reconfigure from QSPI, and on JTAG loads of a second seed AND of the dev-40506026 control build: the LiteX BIOS starts, DDR3 read leveling completes with the window pattern this board always shows, the console prints `Switching SDRAM to hardware control` and then nothing that a boot needs: no memtest, no prompt, no `Milan baremetal` lines. One 140 s capture shows a second BIOS banner beginning after that line and then silence. `scripts/baremetal_uart_smoke.py` times out waiting for `milan_status` on every attempt. The control build stopping identically shows this is not a regression of 3cfc0b81; #358 records the same stall of the persistent baseline and that the board that answers on the bench is a VOLATILE diagnostic image with a clock-domain crossing added between the CPU's DDR AXI port and the memory domain, which is not in the tree.

So the criterion "a booted shipping board demonstrates bare-metal startup, UART/diagnostic access, gPTP ownership, persistence, and audio datapath operation" cannot be met today: startup itself is blocked on that crossing landing in the tree (filed separately, see the linked issue), gPTP lock is #358's open finding (GM absent, pdelay about 1 us), persistence is #70's next step, and audio-datapath evidence needs the controller and capture hosts #358 reports as unreachable. Nothing here is a documentation gap; the card stays Ready.

Bench left as found: the shipping-recipe image set is back in QSPI and the #358 diagnostic bitstream (its published digest, `c0392631...`) is reloaded over JTAG; the grader reads 6 PASS / 4 FAIL exactly as #358 records. Note for anyone at the bench: a power cycle boots the stalling persistent image and discards that working one; I did that three times before reading #358. Build identity (bitstream payload SHA-256 `d930998e...`, AEM `29223ec9...`), the flash transaction logs, every console capture and every grader transcript are retained on the bench workstation per TESTING.md 6b.
The boot-stall defect referenced above is #359.

Update after #359: with PR #361's crossing the shipping image boots from QSPI on a cold power cycle and reaches `Milan baremetal: fabric entity enabled` twice in a row; the UART grader passes identity, publication, AEM, fabric, clock-validity owner and PHC. Of the booted-board criterion that leaves gPTP lock (#358, no grandmaster on this wire), persistence (#70) and audio-datapath operation (needs the controller and capture hosts #358 reports unreachable). Evidence retained on the bench workstation.

title: [Bare-metal] Remove Linux product paths and references from the tracked tree
